newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - Cell Genesys Inc AIDS therapy.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Cell Genesys Inc AIDS therapy.

text.p: Cell Genesys Inc expects to begin releasing Phase II trial results of its AIDS gene therapy in January, chief financial officer Kathleen Glaub told Reuters.
"The Phase Two trials will not actually be complete until the third quarter of 1997 but because the trials are not blinded we have the ability to release interim data before then," Glaub said.
"If the data look promising, we would be in a position to trigger a Phase II/III study by the end of 1997."

Glaub also said the company believes gene therapy could be used to increase the effectivness of drug combinations such as the three-drug "AIDS cocktail," which has recently been shown to dramatically reduce viral load in AIDS patients.
"We were ecstatic like everybody else about the three-drug cocktail," said Glaub. "However, it is still not a cure."
"It's always been our view that while you could use the anti-viral drugs to reduce viral load, our therapy could help extend the useful life of those drugs."
The Cell Genesys therapy aims to genetically modify patients' T-cells so they destroy HIV-infected cells.

Because the company's AIDS research is distinct from its antibody research, Glaub said it plans to reduce ownership of its now wholly-owned Abgenix subsidiary, which was formed last June to develop human monoclonal antibodies for cancer, inflammation and other illnesses.
"Eventually, we'd like to see it go public," she said, adding, "I think we'd want to have its first program in the clinic before (taking it public)."
Abgenix' lead product candidate, anti-interleukin, for inflammation is currently in preclinical studies.
"We feel both our businesses are stand alone businesses. It is difficult to be two companies in one."

Glaub said the company is ending 1996 with a stronger financial position than anticipated. She said it expects to have about $75 million in cash at year end, with the year's cash burn at under $10 million, compared with earlier projections of $18 millin. -Andrea Orr 213 380-2014.
